messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals that belong to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Within Laurasiatheria, lions are part of the order **Carnivora**, while zebras belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (odd‑toed ungulates).  

Their most recent common ancestor would therefore have been a small, early Laurasiatherian mammal that lived during the Paleocene–Eocene epochs (roughly 66–34 million years ago). This ancestor would have possessed the basic mammalian body plan that later gave rise to the diverse lineages of carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
